newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq says Turkish planes kill or injure 20 Kurds.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says Turkish planes kill or injure 20 Kurds.

text.p: Iraq said on Saturday Turkish warplanes bombed villages in northern Iraq, killing or wounding 20 civilian Kurds, and urged non-aligned and Islamic countries to stop the Turkish foray.
"Six Turkish planes bombed villages in the sector of Rawanduz hitting them with rockets and bombs. The bombardment led to the killing and injuring of 20 Iraqi Kurdish civilians," the papers said.

The official Iraqi News Agency (INA) said Foreign Minister Mohammed Saeed al-Sahaf wrote to the non-aligned movement and the Organisation of Islamic Countries demanding action against the Turkish forces. He said Iraq's pleas to the United Nations and the Security Council had gone unanswered.
Thousands of Turkish troops poured into northern Iraq on May 14 in pursuit of separatist Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels who use the region to launch raids into southeast Turkey.

"Iraq called on the non-aligned movement and the Organisation of Islamic conference to shoulder their responsiblity and take a clear stand to stem the continuation of threats and aggression it is subjected to by the Turkish troops," INA, quoting Sahaf, said.
"The United Nations has not taken up to this date any suitable measure to stop the Turkish aggression," Sahaf said, adding the Security Council had also not taken any action.
Iraq has frequently denounced the attack, with Baghdad newspapers saying the invasion was at Washington's behest. Arab countries have also condemned the incursion.
